nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, equipped with its Borel structure and canonical volume, and let S be an arbitrary measurable space. Dimension zero is permitted. Let V:E→ℝ be C² and κ≥1, with
  (1/κ)‖v‖² ≤ D²V(x)[v,v] ≤ ‖v‖²
for all x,v∈E. Let η:S→ℝ and y:S→E be measurable, with η(s)>0 for every s.
There exists a measurable p:S→E such that, for every s,
  p(s)+η(s)∇V(p(s))=y(s),
and every z∈E satisfying z+η(s)∇V(z)=y(s) equals p(s).
Using this same p throughout, define
  ρ_s(u)=V(p(s)+√η(s) u)−V(p(s))−√η(s)⟨∇V(p(s)),u⟩,
  μ=volume.tilted(x↦−V(x)),
  R_s=μ.tilted(x↦−‖x−y(s)‖²/(2η(s))),
  r_s=(x↦(√η(s))⁻¹(x−p(s)))_* R_s,
  γ=the centered covariance-identity Gaussian on E,
  Z_s=∫exp(−ρ_s(u))dγ(u),
  q_s(u)=exp(−ρ_s(u))/Z_s.
Here each tilt is the normalized exponential tilt when its exponential weight is integrable, and the zero measure otherwise. For every s, r_s is absolutely continuous with respect to γ, and its canonical extended-nonnegative-real KL divergence from γ is finite. Its canonical log-likelihood representative llr(r_s,γ) and ρ_s are integrable with respect to r_s. The identity llr(r_s,γ)(u)=log(q_s(u)) holds r_s-almost everywhere. Furthermore,
  KL(r_s‖γ).toReal = ∫q_s(u)log(q_s(u))dγ(u)
                   = −∫ρ_s(u)dr_s(u)−log(Z_s).
The statement supplies p internally, places no upper bound on positive η, and requires no separately supplied stationary selector, probability, normalization, integrability or entropy certificate. The almost-everywhere identity does not assert pointwise equality of the chosen log-likelihood representative.
